# Arrakis Control — Claude Code, Kimi Code and Codex

Extract the archive into the **repository root**, preserving hidden directories (`.claude/`, `.codex/`).

**Before replacing `AGENTS.md`:** compare the included copy against the live repository. The Next.js-managed section is regenerated by Next.js; preserve the live generated version if newer. Avoid overwriting other changes.

- `AGENTS.md`: shared source of truth for all agents.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/`: Claude Code instructions and project permissions.
- `KIMI.md`: optional Kimi companion guide; check whether your Kimi version automatically reads it.
- `.codex/config.toml`: Codex project settings. `CODEX.md` is optional reading, not automatically loaded.

In Claude Code run `claude doctor`, `/status`, and `/model`; confirm the Sonnet version offered by your installation. In Codex, verify active sandbox/approval settings and any higher-priority global configuration before relying on them. Keep approval for Git writes and production operations regardless of the agent.

All tools must read local repository docs and inspect current state; the provided inventory is historical. Permission configuration is not a replacement for isolation and code review.
